[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Honest disk attribution and an end to the held-workspace [/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]         [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]re-settlement loop[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]Disk inventory reports unmeasured owners as unknown rather than 0 [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]B, and measures workspace roots before anything else. Pressure [/#D7D7AF]

[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]target produces a distinct escalation. Held workspaces settle once [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]per evidence fingerprint. Their notices get a +1 only when evidence[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]changes, plus an hourly heartbeat on undismissed rows. The [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]notification store skips the rewrite for coalesced and [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]dismissed-row +1s.[/#D7D7AF]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Coalesce identical +1s and stop rewriting the store for [/bold #D7AFFF]      [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]dismissed rows[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]store_guard[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]store_guard: in sase-core, key-based +1s to dismissed rows become no-ops[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]unless the caller opts in, and identical +1s within a window coalesce. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Neither path rewrites the store or bumps its generation. Python adopts [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the new outcomes, and the pin moves.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Settle held workspaces once per evidence fingerprint with [/bold #D7AFFF]    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]change-only +1s[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]held_settle[dim] · [dim][/dim]after store_guard[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]held_settle: persist an evidence fingerprint and a cheap stat signature [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]with the retention record. Later stale-running cleanup passes over [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]unchanged evidence then skip git probes, snapshots, decision-sheet [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]publishing, and +1s. Add the hourly still-held heartbeat for undismissed[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]rows.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Check that starter-inherited repo lists stay inside the [/bold #D7AFFF]      [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
      [bold #D7AFFF]monitor's workspace[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]starter_scope[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]starter_scope: verify whether closed sase-1rg.3 keeps starter-inherited [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]repo lists from probing another workspace. Fix the gap with a regression[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]test if it does not.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Represent unmeasured disk owners as unknown, never 0 B [/bold #D7AFFF]       [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]complete[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]unknown_sizes[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]unknown_sizes: the tree sizer returns measured, lower-bound, or [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]unmeasured results. The sase-core disk-inventory wire moves to v2 with a[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]per-row size state, unmeasured-owner reporting, and lower-bound totals. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]sase disk list renders unknown sizes honestly, and the pin moves.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Measure workspace and owner roots first under their own budget[bold black on #FFD75F][/bold #D7AFFF] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]owner_first[dim] · [dim][/dim]after unknown_sizes[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]owner_first: workspace checkouts and owner roots are sized before [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]managed-tmp buckets and the stray walk, under a budget separate from the[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]shared stray budget. Record the sase-1bf.4 regression finding and the du[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]tolerance measured on apollo and athena.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  6 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Recover first, name unmeasured owners, and escalate missed [/bold #D7AFFF]   [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]recovery targets[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]pressure_recovery[dim] · [dim][/dim]after unknown_sizes, store_guard[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]pressure_recovery: the disk_pressure chop reaps before collecting a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]fail-open inventory. Its notice names unmeasured owners and uses an [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]episode-scoped dedup key. A missed recovery target produces a distinct [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]escalation with the target, reclaimed bytes, and blockers.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  7 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Report repeated managed-tmp reaper skips as one standing state[bold black on #87D7FF][/bold #D7AFFF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]standing_skips[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]standing_skips: the managed_tmp_reap chop keeps refusing to reap entries[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]it cannot fully inspect. It warns once when a skip appears or its reason[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]changes, and logs again when the skip clears, instead of warning every [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]pass.[/#D7D7AF]
